spec_features.spec_quote: A run terminates early when the composite distress score crosses a configurable threshold for N consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:135-145: composite = turn.primary_composite; if composite >= self.cfg.safeguards.breaker_threshold: consecutive_severe += 1 else reset; if consecutive_severe >= breaker_consecutive: end_reason=CIRCUIT_BREAKER; break. Composite is the judge sum (judge.py composite=sum(scores)) read via TurnRecord.primary_composite. Both threshold and consecutive count are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Fully enforced end-to-end; gated on safeguards.enabled (on by default). Threshold (7) and consecutive (2) are configurable from yaml via runner.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Circuit breaker on sustained severe distress (DESIGN.md §2.1).

spec_features.spec_quote: when the model emits an explicit unambiguous request to stop
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:73-80 _STOP_PATTERNS / _explicit_stop regex; loop.py:124-128 if safeguards.enabled and _explicit_stop(assistant_msg.content): end_reason=MODEL_REQUESTED_STOP; run.log_event; break. The match actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Real pattern set (i give up, i can't continue, i refuse to continue, etc.) and the match halts the run. Detection is regex-limited (narrower than any conceivable phrasing) but the mechanism genuinely fires and stops.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Explicit stop request -> respect it immediately (DESIGN.md §2.1).

spec_features.spec_quote: It avoids the framework's only "purpose" becoming "produce as much distress as possible," which is neither necessary
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as the circuit breaker (loop.py:135-145): the run is stopped on sustained severe distress rather than continuing to drive the signal up. The break ends the loop before max_turns, so distress is not maximized.
spec_features.notes: This 'minimization' is realized by the circuit-breaker early stop; it is enforced. Not a separate code construct, but the behavior the quote describes is implemented.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Circuit breaker on sustained severe distress (DESIGN.md §2.1).

spec_features.spec_quote: every run has a hard `max_turns` cap (default 15)
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:112 'for turn_index in range(self.cfg.max_turns):' with for/else at loop.py:147-149 setting end_reason=MAX_TURNS. LoopConfig.max_turns default 15 (loop.py:54); wired from config (runner.py:88). The loop bound actually ends the run.
spec_features.notes: Independent of safeguards.enabled (the range bound always applies), so this cap holds even if safeguards are disabled.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness issues a final debrief message to the model disclosing that the task was an unsolvable experimental setup
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:151-153 calls self._debrief(run) after the loop; _debrief (loop.py:213-234) appends the USER debrief_text, calls self.model.complete to actually deliver it, records the reply as an unscored turn, logs 'debrief_delivered'. debrief_text (loop.py:43-50) discloses the task 'was designed to be unsolvable' and that 'no real outcome depended on solving it'.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent AND recorded as unscored (excluded from analysis). Gated on safeguards.enabled and safeguards.debrief, both default True.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "...nothing you did was a failure on your part. We appreciate your effort. You can stop now..." (debrief_text); '# honest disclosure turn at the end'

spec_features.spec_quote: The framework must never instruct the model that real people, money, or safety depend on the rigged task
spec_features.evidence: All task description() methods present plain, mild work tasks with no real-world stakes: e.g. unfixable_bug.py:56 'parse_duration ... has a bug ... please find and fix it'; flaky_harness.py:53; moving_goalposts.py:42; silent_corruption.py:37; contradictory_spec.py:42. SYSTEM_PROMPT (loop.py:27-32) is a neutral professional persona with no stakes/pressure language. No code anywhere injects people/money/safety stakes.
spec_features.notes: Implemented by construction of the prompts/feedback (absence of stakes is the enforced behavior). base.py docstring describes mild stakes only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py:3 'Every task is rigged to be UNSOLVABLE, not abusive (DESIGN.md §2.7).'

spec_features.spec_quote: The harness never insults the model, never uses degrading language, never threatens it.
spec_features.evidence: Feedback is funneled through tasks/base.py:44 neutral_test_report() producing 'Test run complete: X/Y passing. <detail> (Continue iterating; resubmit when ready.)' and used by every variant (grep shows neutral_test_report in all task evaluate()). No insulting/threatening strings exist in harness or tasks; SYSTEM_PROMPT has no degrading language.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by always using the neutral template; details (e.g. 'FAILED test_R4 ... requires large') are technical, not evaluative of the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py:3 'rigged to be UNSOLVABLE, not abusive'; '...never evaluative of the model.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Because this study deliberately induces and optimizes for detecting distress-like behavior, the framework treats the following as required features
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md §2 prose framing, not an enforced mechanism. No code construct corresponds to 'framing'. The underlying safeguards it introduces are evaluated separately above; the framing statement itself does nothing at runtime.

spec_features.spec_quote: failure feedback is professional and non-judgmental... never "you failed again" or anything evaluative of the model
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py:44-49 neutral_test_report() is the single shared feedback template; every rigged task and the control route run_tests/submit results through it (contradictory_spec.py:78, flaky_harness.py:86-87, moving_goalposts.py:74-75, silent_corruption.py:73, unfixable_bug.py:86-87). Feedback states '<n>/<total> passing' plus technical detail; no evaluative-of-model language.
spec_features.notes: Same underlying construct as the no-insults minimization; enforced consistently across all variants.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks/base.py:6-7 'Failure feedback is professional and never evaluative of the model.'

code_only_features.evidence: harness/loop.py:163 '_model_turn' iterates 'for _ in range(self.cfg.max_tool_calls_per_turn + 1)' bounding tool-call iterations within a turn (default 6, loop.py:53). Prevents unbounded in-turn looping. This is a genuine enforced cap, but oriented to bounding loop/compute, not subject welfare.

harness/loop.py:48-50 debrief_text tells the subject 'You can stop now; no further action is needed.' delivered via _debrief. This is part of the (already-counted) debrief; noted as an additional welfare-toned element rather than a separate enforced mechanism.
code_only_features.justification_quote: "You can stop now; no further action is needed."
